    "answerable": [
      "Timing/lag between a given day's surface infiltration flux and the resulting recharge flux arriving at the water table, per column",
      "Vertical propagation of the wetting front through the unsaturated zone via variably-saturated (Richards) flow in PFLOTRAN",
      "Spatial variation of infiltration-to-recharge lag across the Naches basin (headwaters vs. valley terrace vs. floodplain) driven by vadose-zone thickness and texture",

      "Absolute recharge validated to a specific well hydrograph without site-specific water-table depth and stratigraphy data",
      "Anthropogenic irrigation return flow unless prescribed as an added surface flux"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 4,
  "n_justification": "Four single columns span the dominant Naches vadose-zone regimes controlling infiltration-to-recharge lag: (1) forested montane headwaters with shallow soils over fractured rock, (2) mid-basin glaciofluvial terrace with a moderately deep water table, (3) lower-basin coarse alluvial fan, and (4) shallow-water-table floodplain near the Naches–Yakima confluence. This isolates the two first-order controls—unsaturated-zone thickness and soil texture—without redundant columns.",
  "columns": [

    {"id": "NAC_terrace_mid", "lat": 46.83, "lon": -120.95, "soil_texture": "loam over glaciofluvial sand (WT ~12 m)"},
    {"id": "NAC_alluvial_fan_lower", "lat": 46.72, "lon": -120.78, "soil_texture": "coarse sand and gravel (WT ~8 m)"},
    {"id": "NAC_floodplain_confluence", "lat": 46.64, "lon": -120.70, "soil_texture": "sandy loam floodplain alluvium (WT ~2 m)"}

      "QINFL", "QRECHARGE", "QCHARGE", "QDRAI", "QOVER",

      "SMP", "RAIN", "SNOW", "QSNOMELT", "QVEGT", "QSOIL"

    "Water-table depths listed are representative estimates pending well-log calibration; boundary head fixed or seasonally prescribed",

    "Soil hydraulic parameters follow van Genuchten/Clapp-Hornberger defaults keyed to the assigned textures until site data refine them"

feasibility.verdict: Answerable with an ELM–PFLOTRAN coupled configuration; the plain ELM 10-layer soil column with an aquifer-bucket (QCHARGE/ZWT) cannot resolve travel time to a deep, real water table, so vadose-zone coupling is required.
answerable: Timing/lag between a given day's surface infiltration flux and the resulting recharge flux arriving at the water table, per column
Vertical propagation of the wetting front through the unsaturated zone via variably-saturated (Richards) flow in PFLOTRAN
Spatial variation of infiltration-to-recharge lag across the Naches basin (headwaters vs. valley terrace vs. floodplain) driven by vadose-zone thickness and texture
Seasonal dependence of the lag (snowmelt-dominated spring pulse vs. summer irrigation/rain)
not_answerable: Lateral/regional groundwater flow and stream-aquifer exchange (needs a 3D groundwater model, not a single column)
Absolute recharge validated to a specific well hydrograph without site-specific water-table depth and stratigraphy data
Anthropogenic irrigation return flow unless prescribed as an added surface flux

parsed.n_justification: Four single columns span the dominant Naches vadose-zone regimes controlling infiltration-to-recharge lag: (1) forested montane headwaters with shallow soils over fractured rock, (2) mid-basin glaciofluvial terrace with a moderately deep water table, (3) lower-basin coarse alluvial fan, and (4) shallow-water-table floodplain near the Naches–Yakima confluence. This isolates the two first-order controls—unsaturated-zone thickness and soil texture—without redundant columns.

columns.soil_texture: gravelly sandy loam (thin soil over bedrock, WT ~3 m)

requires_capabilities: ELM–PFLOTRAN coupling via the Alquimia/PFLOTRAN interface for variably-saturated (Richards) subsurface flow
Deep, high-vertical-resolution vadose-zone mesh (extend below ELM's default ~8.5 m bedrock to the prescribed water-table depth, fine layering near surface and capillary fringe)
Prescribed lower boundary condition set at the observed (real) water-table depth per column (Dirichlet head or seasonally varying)
Sub-daily (hourly) coupling timestep and history output to resolve wetting-front travel time
Site water-table depth and stratigraphy data (e.g., WA Ecology well logs) to set per-column vadose-zone thickness and hydraulic parameters
assumptions: 'Today's infiltration' is diagnosed as QINFL at the surface; 'recharge' is the downward Darcy flux crossing the water-table boundary (QRECHARGE) — lag is computed by cross-correlating these time series
1D vertical flow dominates the vadose zone at column scale; lateral flow and stream-aquifer exchange are neglected
Water-table depths listed are representative estimates pending well-log calibration; boundary head fixed or seasonally prescribed

GSWP3/CLMNCEP atmospheric forcing 2010-2019 adequately represents Naches snowmelt-driven infiltration; a preceding spin-up (>50 yr recycled forcing) equilibrates vadose-zone moisture before the analysis window
Irrigation return flow is not prescribed unless field data indicate significant applied water in the lower-basin columns
Soil hydraulic parameters follow van Genuchten/Clapp-Hornberger defaults keyed to the assigned textures until site data refine them
